ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is the unregulated DC input power supply Vi; the upper end of the power supply passes through the top series resistor Rs and then reaches the output node on the right side. Between this output node and the lower return line, two branches are connected in parallel: one is the Zener diode branch, marked with regulated voltage Vz; the other is the load resistor R0. Therefore, Rs supplies power in series, and the Zener diode and R0 are both connected in parallel across the two ends of the output terminal. Reasoning: The problem gives Vz = 5 V, Vi,min = 6 V, Vi,max = 8 V, Rs = 6 Ω, and Zener maximum power dissipation Pz,max = 2.5 W. To find the minimum R0, it is necessary to consider that regulation can still be maintained when the load current is maximum. At the minimum input voltage, the series resistor current is minimum; at this time, if a 5 V output is still maintained, then Is = (Vi,min - Vz) / Rs = (6 - 5) / 6 = 1/6 A. When R0 takes the minimum value, the load current is maximum, and the ideal Zener is just at the conduction boundary, Iz = 0, therefore IL = Is = 1/6 A. Thus R0 = Vz / IL = 5 / (1/6) = 30 Ω. Therefore the minimum R0 is 30 Ω.
